text:
eva: Heads up — after the kernel selection roll last night we saw a small but consistent p95/p99 bump on a subset of prefix-cache hits. p99 up ~6% on stable workload. :eyes:
jamie: ugh. same cohort as the batching alignment change?
micah: yeah the rollout flipped some kernel affinity heuristics for short-prefix runs, could affect batch packing and therefore KV eviction timing.
eva: my hypothesis: prompt header ordering (the service injects a few metadata headers) changed canonicalization, so keys are slightly different and warmup hit rates dropped. unpacking looks like: key_fingerprint = sha256(prefix + headers_sorted?) vs previous sort-by-insert-order.
sahil: do we have an example pair? can we repro locally with the warmup harness?
eva: repro snippet I used: `prefix = "USER: Hi\n"; headers_old = "X-Model:guppy X-Tier:dedicated"; headers_new = "X-Tier:dedicated X-Model:guppy"` — hits differ. old engine treated header order as stable, new canonicalizer sorts, so fingerprint changed.
jamie: wait, canonicalizing should be good long term. why does kernel bump correlate?
micah: two effects: (1) canonicalization change created a short-lived decrease in cache hit rate (different keys), (2) kernel selection changed batching so warmup windows were shorter — together they amplify hit-rate drop.
eva: perf-bot trace shows more frequent KV backfills within the same request window after the rollout. attaching timeline: `warmup: 120ms -> cache-miss -> first-token 190ms` vs pre-roll `warmup: 90ms -> hit -> first-token 110ms`.
sahil: can we roll-forward a quick patch to accept both canonical forms for a transition window? maybe map old fingerprints to new normalized fingerprints on lookup.
micah: feasible — add a fallback probe: on miss, check `legacy_fingerprint(prefix + raw_headers)` for a hit before doing full compute. cheap-ish.
jamie: downside: double-lookup could add overhead on cold hits, but it's only on miss paths which are already expensive.
eva: alternative: backfill a translation table during warmup (one-time background job) that maps legacy -> canonical for active prefixes. avoids per-request penalty.
sahil: how to seed the table? run warmup harness against live traffic samples and generate mappings. need to watch memory pressure.
jamie: memory estimate? if we map 200k active keys churny cohort it might be a few hundred MBs of metadata — fine for dedicated pools but not for smaller hosts.
micah: we can make it opt-in per-pool: Dedicated gets backfill; Shared fallback remains single-lookup only.
eva: kernel-side fix: revert the batching alignment changes that shortened warmup window until we have mapping in place? risky.
jamie: I'd rather do mapping + canary of translation table for one region, measure hit-rate recovery. then decide if kernel rollback needed.
perf-bot: perf regression alert: p99 latency +6% (cohort A) — tag: warmup/key-churn — seen in eu-west-1 canary.
sahil: ok plan: (1) implement lazy fallback fingerprint probe (micah) (2) run warmup backfill job for dedicated pools (eva+jamie) (3) monitor hit-rate and p99 for 24h canary (sahil)
micah: I'll open a tiny PR for fallback probe w/ opt-in flag and perf guard. ETA EOD.
eva: I'll wire up sampling job and start backfill in staging.
jamie: create a dashboard slice for cohort A vs control showing hit-rate, first-token latency, and KV lookups. want to see if double-lookup cost is negligible.
sahil: if mapping + fallback recovers >=90% of lost hit-rate we keep kernel change. if not, we consider rollback.
eva: one more note: system prompts are also sometimes being rewritten by the agent layer -> they must be normalized the same way. I'll add a lint rule in the ingestion path so we don't accidentally reorder those fields.
micah: great. also add a unit test that ensures fingerprint stability across canonicalizer changes (legacy -> normalized equivalence).
jamie: thanks all — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
